comparator.name: Business Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme pages establish a coherent 180-EC Business Administration pathway: a fixed 60-EC first year, a fixed 60-EC second year applicable from 2025-2026, and a third year applicable from 2026-2027 with 18 EC of compulsory advanced business study, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The third-year free space may be filled with courses, a coherent minor, study abroad or a 12- or 24-EC internship. The programme has no formal named route that must be selected, so the genuine choice space is preserved rather than instantiated for UCR fit.
components: Introduction to Behaviour in Organisations and Work

alternatives.label: Business administration, organisations & strategy
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Business Administration programme combining organisations and change, strategy, marketing, entrepreneurship, leadership and people management with accounting, finance, economics, qualitative and quantitative research, data, technology and international governance.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum integrates organisational behaviour and leadership with strategy, marketing, entrepreneurship, accounting, finance, economics, research, technology and international governance.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, leadership and communication foundations precede advanced strategy, marketing, organisational psychology, econometrics, market research and international governance. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Business analytics & digital transformation
alternatives.concept: A business route organised around analytics, artificial intelligence and digital transformation, combining programming, databases, mathematics, statistics, machine learning and deep learning with strategy, organisations, marketing, economics, governance and responsible AI.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines business strategy, organisations, marketing and economics with programming, databases, mathematics, statistics, machine learning, deep learning, algorithms and responsible AI.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces substantial leadership, finance, qualitative-research and entrepreneurship content with programming, databases, linear algebra, probability, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning and AI ethics. Ten of the 24 courses differ, and digital analytics becomes the programme's organising logic.
progression: Business, programming, data, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced strategy, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning, international business and market research. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, probability and deep learning; programming precedes algorithms. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Responsible entrepreneurship & sustainable strategy
alternatives.concept: A business route organised around responsible entrepreneurship and sustainable strategy, combining business foundations, economics, marketing, leadership and research with climate, circular economy, sustainable innovation, governance, remediation and renewable-system design.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines business, entrepreneurship, strategy and leadership with a sustained sequence in sustainability, circular economy, sustainable innovation, governance and system design.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad and digital routes, this curriculum gives sustained weight to climate, circular economy, sustainability science, ecological innovation, environmental governance, remediation and renewable-system design. Ten courses differ from the closest programme and fourteen from the digital route, making responsible and sustainable entrepreneurship the governing academic direction.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes advanced circular-resource and renewable-system work; business and research foundations precede advanced law, public economics, leadership and market research, with all formal prerequisites completed earlier.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers organisational functioning and change, strategy, marketing, people, responsible management, finance, economics and empirical research. Two additional stable, generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible: business analytics and digital expertise; and entrepreneurship, innovation and sustainable strategy. Each differs from the closest programme by ten courses, and they differ from each other by fourteen courses, so each exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor and represents a different academic organising logic. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both address the design and improvement of production processes; UCR does so through an applied product-development project.
Both introduce strategic analysis and organisational response to changing markets; UCR adds digital transformation.
Both develop entrepreneurship through venture design, market validation and business planning; UCR explicitly includes social entrepreneurship.
UCR offers strategy and strategic-thinking courses but no separate advanced strategy course in the selected curricula.
Both address strategic people management, diversity and inclusion in organisations.
Both examine behaviour, motivation and leadership within organisations; UCR uses organisational psychology as its frame.
Both develop strategic analysis and decision-making; UCR emphasises negotiation and strategic interaction.
UCR studies organisations and leadership across several courses but has no single dedicated organisation-theory counterpart.
UCR covers organisational behaviour, strategy and leadership but has no dedicated organisation-design course.
UCR addresses organisational change across strategy, leadership and digital-transformation courses, but no single dedicated course reproduces this component.
UCR has no dedicated organisational systems-theory course in the current enriched catalogue.
Both develop accounting knowledge and the use of financial reporting for organisational decisions.
Both develop financial analysis, risk assessment and corporate decision-making.
Both introduce economic reasoning about firms, markets and the wider economy.
Both provide advanced quantitative analysis for organisational questions; UCR focuses on econometric estimation and inference.
Both examine marketing strategy, consumer behaviour and responsible customer engagement.
Both require students to design and conduct empirical research on an organisational or market problem; UCR's project is course-based rather than a separate thesis.
Both introduce research design, statistics and quantitative analysis.
Both develop qualitative research design, data collection, interpretation and methodological reflexivity.
UCR combines data, research and responsible-management courses, but no single scheduled course reproduces this integrated business-analysis component.
Both analyse how digital technologies and AI reshape organisations, innovation and managerial decisions.
Both examine governance and responsibility across organisations and society; UCR focuses specifically on sustainability governance.
Both develop academic source use, argument, communication, collaboration and reflective professional skills.
Both develop normative reasoning about responsibility, values and contested organisational decisions.
This is genuine free-choice space. UCR flexibility is distributed across the complete 180-EC curriculum, so no single scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: Both programmes cover organisations, strategy, marketing, people, finance, economics, research, digital change and responsible management. Radboud additionally requires a dense functional sequence in organisation theory and design, operations and logistics, systems theory, qualitative and quantitative methods, and a separate bachelor thesis, while preserving 30 EC of free-choice space. UCR can build coherent business, digital-analytics and responsible-entrepreneurship programmes, but it does not reproduce every specialist organisational component as a dedicated course.
